sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects

items.q: Match the following membrane events — 1) Basolateral iodide entry 2) Apical iodide movement 3) TSH signal … A) Cl–I exchange by pendrin B) Na–I symport C) cAMP increase
items.exp: The schematic places NIS basolaterally, pendrin at the apical iodide pathway and TSH receptor signaling through cAMP. (Book p900)

items.q: The immediate second-messenger rise shown after TSH receptor binding is ___.
items.exp: The synthesis diagram labels increased cAMP below TSH receptor binding. (Book p900)

items.q: A transport defect prevents entry of iodide from blood into the follicular cell. Which transporter is primarily affected?
items.exp: NIS traps iodide across the basolateral membrane; pendrin acts later at the apical side. (Book p900)

items.q: Match the following synthetic components — 1) TPO 2) DUOX2 3) Thyroglobulin … A) Thyroid peroxidase B) Tyrosine-rich scaffold C) Hydrogen-peroxide-generating system
items.exp: TPO drives oxidation/organification and coupling using oxidizing equivalents supplied by DUOX2; thyroglobulin provides tyrosyl residues. (Book p900)

items.q: At the apical thyroid interface, which system is required for iodination of thyroglobulin tyrosyl residues?
opts: Type II deiodinase with reduced glutathione
items.exp: Thyroid hormone organification requires TPO and hydrogen peroxide; the handwritten enzyme-independent label should not be learned as established physiology. (Book p900)

items.q: Coupling MIT with DIT yields ___, while DIT with DIT yields ___.
items.exp: The diagram gives MIT + DIT = T3 and DIT + DIT = T4 during coupling on thyroglobulin. (Book p900)

items.q: A synthetic defect leaves iodinated thyroglobulin available but prevents the coupling reaction. Which enzyme is most directly implicated?
items.exp: TPO participates in coupling iodotyrosines as well as the earlier oxidation/organification chemistry. (Book p900)

items.q: Match the following ordered events — 1) Colloid uptake into follicular cell 2) Proteolysis 3) Peripheral conversion … A) Release from thyroglobulin B) Retrieval of stored iodinated protein C) T4 converted to active T3
items.exp: The later diagram steps are uptake of stored thyroglobulin, proteolysis and release, followed by peripheral conversion of T4. (Book p900)

items.q: The source labels T4:T3 as ___ in the follicular stored material and ___ at hormone release.
items.exp: These are the two ratios printed at successive locations in the diagram; they are not interchangeable labels for a measured free-hormone serum ratio. (Book p900)

items.q: Evaluate iodide's acute effect in the release diagram: I An inhibitory arrow points from iodide to hormone release. II This means more iodide always increases immediate hormone release.
items.exp: The diagram marks acute iodide inhibition of release; iodine effects vary with dose, timing and underlying thyroid disease. (Book p900)

items.q: Only a minority of circulating T3 is secreted directly by the thyroid. Which source distribution best explains the remainder?
items.exp: The page assigns 80% to peripheral conversion and 20% to direct synthesis, emphasizing T4-to-T3 conversion. (Book p900)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among non-thyroid NIS-expressing tissues listed?
items.exp: The source's 'silent' tissue list names salivary gland, breast and placenta. NIS expression does not imply thyroid-hormone production in these sites. (Book p900)

items.q: A nodule has reduced radionuclide uptake. Which conclusion avoids the source's overly broad 'cold nodule (malignant)' label?
opts: Both benign and malignant nodules can be cold
Every cold nodule is a carcinoma
Every cold nodule is an autonomous toxic adenoma
items.exp: Reduced NIS expression/uptake can occur in adenoma or carcinoma; a cold scan is not a histologic diagnosis of malignancy. (Book p900)

items.q: Match the following inhibitors and steps — 1) Perchlorate/thiocyanate 2) Acute excess iodide 3) TPO inhibition … A) Impaired organification/coupling B) Reduced release C) Reduced iodide trapping
items.exp: Perchlorate and thiocyanate compete at iodide uptake; excess iodide acutely inhibits release; TPO inhibition affects organification and coupling. (Book p900)

items.q: Assess iodide-uptake blockers: I Perchlorate and thiocyanate inhibit NIS-mediated uptake. II Both are routine first-line treatments for every form of amiodarone thyrotoxicosis.
items.exp: The pharmacologic uptake inhibition is useful to learn, but thiocyanate is not a routine treatment and perchlorate use is restricted by toxicity and setting. (Book p900)

items.q: A child has goiter and sensorineural hearing loss with an autosomal-recessive apical iodide-transport defect. Which diagnosis fits?
items.exp: Pendred syndrome involves pendrin, a chloride–iodide exchanger, with goiter and SNHL; the source spells it 'Pendrin syndrome.' (Book p900)

items.q: Pendred syndrome's inheritance pattern is ___, and the transporter exchanges ___ with iodide.
items.exp: The source labels the pendrin defect AR and identifies Cl−/I− antiport, distinct from the sodium–iodide symporter. (Book p900)
